archetypes.name: Distrustful routine skeptics
archetypes.text: People who say you can't be too careful with others yet still check political information online, and who feel mostly unenthused about politics and democracy while staying pretty happy overall. They report a stalled, below-average family income and see themselves as lower class, but rate the economy as neither good nor bad and keep close ties with relatives. Their unusual mix is strong unease about robots and AI paired with ordinary, mid-level views on science spending and technology, so their worries about automation sit oddly beside their calm, routine outlook on life.

archetypes.name: Distrustful disengaged skeptics
archetypes.text: People who combine deep distrust of others and institutions with political withdrawal and dissatisfaction, yet feel personally content with their happiness and family life. They rate the economy harshly and see taxes as too high, but their own finances feel stable. Their social lives are mostly routine and low-key, with occasional family and friend contact. They hold mixed views on technology and AI, ranging from worry to ambivalence, which sits oddly beside their otherwise firm stances on work-family issues.

archetypes.name: Politically disengaged but content
archetypes.text: These respondents report low trust in institutions and dissatisfaction with how democracy works, yet describe their personal finances and happiness positively. They show little interest in politics and rarely verify online political information, while still feeling the economy is good. Their social lives mix frequent family contact with few evening outings with friends outside the neighborhood. Views on technology and AI are split, and they often withhold strong opinions, combining personal contentment with institutional skepticism in a way that cuts against typical civic engagement patterns.

archetypes.name: Distrustful economic pessimists
archetypes.text: These respondents combine deep distrust of other people and institutions with a sense that their own finances have slipped, even though their self-described standing is middling. Their pessimism about democracy and the economy runs alongside an unusual enthusiasm for technology and a sharp split on AI, where some are unbothered while others are very worried. They also sense a dull, routine life, yet many still value scientific spending and do not see taxes as clearly excessive. Their outlook is wary and withdrawn, but not uniformly hostile to change.
